source: Seeded from gcse-science/y10 lesson 84 (Eye diagram labelling sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 84: The eye: a receptor organ. To understand how the structures of the eye let it focus light and respond to light intensity

picture.draw: Draw and label: Eye diagram labelling sheet

questions.q: Explain how the eye responds when you walk into bright sunlight.
questions.a: Receptors in retina detect bright light (1); circular muscles of iris contract, radial relax (1); pupil gets smaller, less light enters, protecting the retina (1)
questions.model: Stimulus: bright light, detected by the retina. Effector: iris muscles. Circular contract, radial relax. Response: smaller pupil.

questions.q: Explain how the eye changes to focus on a book after looking at a distant tree. Portal response box.
questions.a: Ciliary muscles contract (1); suspensory ligaments slacken (1); lens becomes fatter/more rounded (1); refracts light more (1); light focused on the retina (1); image clear (1)
questions.model: Teacher writes: 'To focus on the near book, the ciliary muscles contract.'

questions.q: Why is the pupil reflex a reflex and not a conscious action?
questions.a: Automatic and fast (1); does not involve conscious thought; protects the retina (1)

questions.q: Long-sightedness: the lens cannot become fat enough. Suggest which objects look blurred and why.
questions.a: Near objects: light is focused behind the retina.

questions.q: Big question: how does the eye focus near then far?
questions.a: Ciliary muscles change the lens: fatter for near, thinner for far.
